test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following countries is the largest producer of gold in the world in 2019?
solution:
The correct answer is **China.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gold mining is a global business with operations on every continent, except Antarctica, and gold is extracted from mines of widely varying types and scale
 
• At a country level, **China** was the largest producer in the world and accounted for around 9 percent of total global production

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An estimated **100 metric tons** of gold were produced in South Africa. The gold mining industry in South Africa is an important source of employment. India's gold mine production.
 
• Australia is the** second largest gold producer in the world**, reaching **390 tonnes per annum**. Australia has two of the world's 20 largest gold mines and reserves totaling more than 380 million ounces of gold
 
• India's gold mine production is just **1.6 tonnes as of 2019** and could rise to 20 tonnes per year, highlights a World Gold Council report on 'Gold Mining in India".
